query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating DSC with in-situ neutron imaging will yield accurate, direct measurements of the melting temperature, fusion enthalpy/entropy, and volume change for equiatomic HEAs with an uncertainty lower than 5% compared to established reference alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: A set of well-characterized equiatomic high-entropy alloys, such as the Cantor alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) and selected refractory HEAs.
generation.intervention: Perform differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) experiments concurrently with in-situ neutron imaging using a high-temperature furnace that allows incremental heating (e.g., 10 K steps) and controlled relaxation between steps.
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure under inert gas flow (Ar or N2) with a heating rate of approximately 10 K/min, extending from room temperature up to 1.2–1.5 times the expected melting point.
generation.structural_mediator: Real-time imaging contrast between crystalline and liquid phases via neutron transmission differences, corroborated by DSC endothermic/exothermic peaks.
generation.mechanism: The combined approach exploits the thermal energy input (DSC) to trigger phase transitions while in-situ imaging directly visualizes atomic rearrangement and volume expansion, enabling cross-correlation for accurate thermodynamic determination.
generation.predicted_outcome: Fusion properties (melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, and volume change) will be determined with a precision within ±5% of reference values; imaging will reveal distinct pre-melting and full-melting stages consistent with the measured DSC peaks.
generation.baseline: Conventional DSC or DTA experiments performed without simultaneous imaging typically yield uncertainties of 10% or more and may miss gradual pre-melting behavior.
generation.boundary: This approach is expected to be valid for alloys exhibiting clear phase boundary contrasts; it may be less effective where liquid-phase segregation or amorphization smears the DSC signal.
generation.uncertainty: Instrumental calibration accuracy, image resolution during high-temperature operation, and potential signal interference from grain-boundary effects in polycrystalline samples.

falsification_experiment.design: Test a series of HEAs using the combined DSC/in-situ neutron imaging setup and compare the fusion property measurements against independently validated standard reference materials and conventional DSC data.
measurements: DSC endothermic/exothermic peak temperatures and areas
Neutron imaging contrast profiles and phase boundary movement
Calculated volume change from diffraction or imaging data
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the combined method yields fusion property values that deviate by more than ±10% compared to independently validated standards or fails to capture distinct pre-melting and melting stage signals, the approach would be ruled out.

cited_evidence.text: The calculation of configurational entropy, also called mixing entropy, is given in Equation (3) with n as the number of elements, xi the concentration of each element i and R as the universal gas constant. The equation is derived from the mixing of noble gases and is adopted to fully disordered solid solution, which are assumed in our work. If elements are distributed non-equally between possible sub-lattices, then a more general equation should be used []. In case of an equiatomic alloy, Equation (3) is reduced to ΔSconf=Rlnn. Thus the configurational entropy of 5-component equiatomic alloy is ~1.6·R. At 0 K the resulting total entropy may not be zero. This does not violate the third law of thermodynamics (dSdT|T=0=0) which is often misinterpreted as S(T = 0) = 0. Crystalline solids may exhibit a non-zero entropy at the absolute zero point due to a randomly crystallographic orientation. A change of entropy in this point is not possible, because there is no ability of motion or diffusion. The field of high-entropy alloys continues to grow every year, and with this growth comes an enormous amount of never before seen alloy systems with unknown liquid state behavior. As previously shown, neutron imaging can be a very useful technique to elucidate the liquid state behavior of molten alloy systems. With the application of this technique to high-entropy alloys, in-situ imaging of liquid state miscibility has been observed for the first time with the equiatomic additions of Ni to the immiscible CoCrCu system. The current results show the following: Neutron imaging can be utilized to image liquid state behavior in high-entropy alloys. Imaging was carried out on equiatomic CoCrCu buttons with equiatomic additions of Ni such that when melting occurred between the alloying elements, full miscibility was achieved. In-situ neutron imaging was successfully utilized to image in-situ alloying of Ni into an immiscible CoCrCu system. The synthesis of the CoCrCuNi alloy inside the high-temperature furnace was fully imaged via a movie-like sequence of carefully timed radiographs to display the melting/alloying process. papers.title: How atoms of polycrystalline Nb20.6Mo21.7Ta15.6W21.1V21.0 refractory high-entropy alloys rearra
papers.system: Refractory high-entropy alloy Nb20.6Mo21.7Ta15.6W21.1V21.0 (single crystal and polycrystalline)
papers.approach: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation using the 2NN MEAM potential with systematic temperature elevation and grain size variation
papers.findings: Identified a two‐stage melting process in polycrystalline samples: initial grain-boundary pre‐melting at a lower temperature, then complete melting at the system-melting point. In single crystals, an abrupt density drop and enthalpy change occurred between 2910 and 2940 K.
papers.mechanism: Melting is driven by local atomic rearrangement and chemical short-range order changes; grain boundaries melt first, inducing rearrangement in adjacent grains.

papers.title: Entropy Determination of Single-Phase High Entropy Alloys with Different Crystal Structures over a Wide Temperature Range.
papers.system: Various single-phase high-entropy alloys (fcc, bcc, hcp; including equiatomic alloys such as fcc-Cantor and crystalline nickel)
papers.approach: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to measure temperature-dependent heat capacity (cp(T)) across a wide range (from −170 °C up to the solidus) and application of the rule of mixtures for the Dulong–Petit comparison
papers.findings: Thermal entropy extracted from cp(T) integrates to yield the major contribution to total entropy, while configurational entropy provides a vertical offset. Melting enthalpy and entropy contributions to Gibbs free energy are quantified.
papers.mechanism: The measured heat capacities align with the Dulong–Petit law at room temperature; integration of cp(T) results in the thermal entropy, and the configurational contribution is determined by alloy complexity.

papers.title: Computational property predictions of Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr high-entropy alloys.
papers.approach: Hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) simulations to evaluate changes in enthalpy, entropy, and Gibbs free energy during an annealing (MC/MD swap) process
papers.findings: Observed a continuous decrease in ΔG with increasing MC swaps and convergence when chemical ordering develops. Configurational entropy contributes nearly 40% relative to enthalpy change due to local chemical clustering.
papers.mechanism: Simulated structure evolution reflects local chemical ordering (short-range clustering) which lowers the free energy through both enthalpic and entropic contributions.

papers.title: Predictive multiphase evolution in Al-containing high-entropy alloys.
papers.system: Al-containing high-entropy alloys with multiphase microstructures
papers.approach: High-throughput Monte Carlo simulations guided by first-principles parameters, combined with calorimetry, in situ microscopy, and neutron scattering to capture phase transitions including melting
papers.findings: Successfully reproduced key features of phase evolution such as intermetallic formation and solid–liquid separation; matched predicted transition temperatures with experimental DSC and scattering data.
papers.mechanism: The model uses computed enthalpy and entropy contributions (both mixing and formation) to determine Gibbs free energy for phase stability, with melting behavior emerging from energy minimization.

papers.title: Thermal Analysis of High-Entropy Rare Earth Oxides.
papers.system: High-entropy rare earth sesquioxides (equimolar mixtures of La, Sm, Dy, Er with Nd, Gd or Y)
papers.approach: Experimental techniques including splat quenching, high-temperature differential thermal analysis (DTA), synchrotron XRD, combined with CALPHAD modeling to extract fusion enthalpy, volume change, and melting temperature
papers.findings: Measured unit cell volumes, volume changes at phase transitions, and a melting point that is higher than any constituent oxide; CALPHAD predictions aligned with experimental fusion enthalpy values.
papers.mechanism: Non-ideal mixing (both in the solid and liquid states) leads to modified melting behavior and fusion enthalpy values compared to constituent oxides.

papers.title: Thermal and Structural Analysis of a High-Entropy Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 Alloy-Infl
papers.approach: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) combined with microstructural characterization (XRD, SEM, TEM, Mössbauer spectroscopy) to analyze endothermic and exothermic peaks during heating and cooling
papers.findings: Identified distinct DSC endothermic peaks corresponding to fusion and melting transitions, with quantified energy absorptions; established melting onset, peak, and exothermic crystallization signatures.
papers.mechanism: DSC peak features map to latent heat absorption during fusion and release during crystallization, reflecting the energy change associated with phase transformations.

papers.title: Microstructure and Thermal Analysis of Metastable Intermetallic Phases in High-Entropy Alloy CoCrFeMo0.85Ni.
papers.approach: Combined differential thermal analysis (DTA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to extract phase transition temperatures, solidus/liquidus, and fusion enthalpy, supported by microstructural (SEM/EDX) characterization
papers.findings: Determined transition temperatures (e.g., melting and formation of intermetallics) with close comparison to CALPHAD predictions; established a primary crystallization window for the FCC phase.
papers.mechanism: Thermal signals (kinks and peaks) in DTA/DSC are attributed to intermetallic formation and melting events driven by changes in enthalpy and configurational order.

papers.title: In-Situ Imaging of Molten High-Entropy Alloys Using Cold Neutrons.
papers.system: High-entropy alloys based on CoCrCu with equiatomic additions of Ni
papers.approach: In-situ neutron imaging using a high-temperature furnace and cold neutrons to directly observe liquid state behavior during melting and alloying
papers.findings: Captured real-time segregation and subsequent remixing of immiscible liquid phases; demonstrated that the addition of Ni enables full miscibility visualized via distinct neutron transmission contrasts.
papers.mechanism: Differences in neutron absorption among alloying elements allow visualization of phase separation and recombination in the liquid state, confirming predicted miscibility changes.

papers.title: Third-Generation Thermodynamic Descriptions for Ta-Cr and Ta-V Binary Systems.
papers.approach: Development of third-generation Gibbs energy expressions incorporating thermal vacancy contributions and two-state models for the liquid, combined with CALPHAD assessment
papers.findings: Achieved excellent agreement between calculated and experimental heat capacity (Cp) and Gibbs energies over a wide temperature range; reliably captured melting behavior and thermal vacancies near the melting point.
papers.mechanism: Inclusion of thermal vacancy effects and a two-state liquid model enhances the description of lattice stability and fusion properties across the temperature range.

papers.title: Accelerated exploration of multi-principal element alloys with solid solution phases.
papers.system: Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) spanning a broad compositional space
papers.approach: High-throughput CALPHAD calculations leveraging binary and ternary phase diagram data to assess phase stability and thermodynamic properties, including melting and fusion behavior
papers.findings: Rapidly screened over 100,000 compositions to identify stable solid solution phases at high temperatures; demonstrated the effectiveness of CALPHAD to predict phase diagrams in complex alloys.
papers.mechanism: Utilizes constituent thermodynamic data to build phase diagrams and apply Gibbs free energy minimization, correlating mixing enthalpy/entropy with phase stability.

papers.title: Thermodynamics-Guided High-Throughput Discovery of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloys for Rapid Solidification.
papers.approach: Composition screening using empirical criteria (atomic size mismatch δr and valence electron concentration VEC) combined with ThermoCalc/CALPHAD evaluations to predict melting, enthalpy, and liquid-phase properties
papers.findings: Defined narrow composition ranges that balance eutectic formation with avoidance of unwanted amorphous phases; provided direction for rapidly solidified alloys with targeted liquid properties.
papers.mechanism: Empirical thresholds based on δr and VEC guide selection of compositions that optimize the interplay between mixing enthalpy and configurational entropy, thereby tuning melting behavior.

papers.title: The Effect of Zr Addition on Melting Temperature, Microstructure, Recrystallization and Mechanical Properties of a Cantor High Entropy Alloy.
papers.system: Cantor alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) and Zr-modified CoCrFeMnNiZr high-entropy alloys
papers.approach: Vacuum induction melting combined with DSC and microstructural characterization to assess melting temperatures, phase morphology and recrystallization behavior
papers.findings: The addition of 5 at.% Zr significantly lowered the melting temperature due to eutectic formation, resulting in enhanced homogenization and finer grain size upon casting.
papers.mechanism: Eutectic interactions between Zr and other elements reduce the activation barrier for melting, thereby lowering the overall melting temperature.

established: Calorimetric techniques (DSC/DTA) reliably capture cp(T) from which thermal entropy and melting enthalpy can be derived.
MD and hybrid MC/MD simulations can reproduce atomic-scale melting behavior and quantify enthalpic and entropic contributions.
CALPHAD-based approaches using thermodynamic databases can predict phase stability, fusion properties, and melting temperatures in complex alloys.
In-situ techniques such as neutron imaging provide real-time visualization of liquid phase behavior.

approaches_tried.outcome: Resolved two-stage melting with grain-boundary pre-melting and bulk melting; effective for refractory HEAs.
Accurate measurement of cp(T), fusion enthalpy/entropy, and detection of melting onset/peak temperatures across various HEA systems.
Captured free energy evolution and equilibrium states reflecting contributions from both enthalpy and configurational entropy.
Efficient prediction of phase diagrams, melting properties, and composition ranges for stable solid solutions in multi-component alloys.
Visualized liquid phase separation and remixing in real time, confirming miscibility changes.

mechanisms: Atomic-scale rearrangements during heating cause abrupt density and enthalpy changes at melting.
Grain-boundary pre-melting initiates bulk melting in polycrystalline HEAs.
Configurational entropy (mixing entropy) markedly stabilizes the high-entropy solid solution phases.
Thermal vacancies and two-state liquid behavior contribute to the overall free energy near fusion.
disagreements: Some discrepancies exist between CALPHAD-predicted transition temperatures and those measured via DSC/DTA in certain HEA systems.
Differences in estimated formation enthalpies (using proxies like Hmix versus directly computed Hf) can lead to uncertainties in phase predictions.
open_questions: How to integrate multi-scale simulations (atomistic and thermodynamic) to predict fusion properties accurately across the vast HEA compositional space.
The range of applicability of each method (MD, DSC, CALPHAD, neutron imaging) for different alloy families and grain sizes.
How refinements in interatomic potentials and thermodynamic databases can further improve predictions of enthalpy, entropy, and volume changes at melting.
opportunities: Combining high-throughput CALPHAD screening with machine learning and experimental DSC/MD validation to quickly map fusion properties across diverse HEA systems.
Extending in-situ imaging techniques to capture dynamic melting behavior in real time for correlation with simulation outputs.
Exploring the influence of minor alloying additions (like Zr) to tune fusion properties and validate eutectic formation effects.
Developing unified thermodynamic models that incorporate both configurational and vibrational entropy effects for a comprehensive description of liquid-phase behavior.

directions.direction: Integrate high-resolution calorimetry (DSC/DTA) with in-situ imaging (neutron or synchrotron XRD) to capture melting transitions, fusion enthalpy/entropy, and volume changes in HEAs in real time.
directions.assessment: This approach directly measures fusion properties with spatially resolved data. It builds on established DSC and in-situ imaging techniques (e.g., PMC7513177, PMC8320920) while offering enhanced precision. It is well supported by known physics, though the integration across a wide HEA family may require careful design of the sample environment and calibration.

directions.direction: Use multi-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) simulations enhanced by improved interatomic potentials to predict melting temperature, enthalpy/entropy changes, and volume change at melting.
directions.assessment: Atomistic simulations allow determination of atomic rearrangements and phase transitions with detailed potential energy analysis. They are strongly supported by previous studies (e.g., PMC8956691, PMC7921137) but must be calibrated carefully to ensure quantitative accuracy over diverse HEA chemistries.

directions.direction: Deploy high-throughput CALPHAD calculations integrated with machine learning algorithms for rapid prediction and optimization of liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in a vast HEA compositional space.
directions.assessment: CALPHAD has been successful in predicting phase stability (PMC4366518, PMC11336915) and, when augmented with ML, can efficiently screen large compositional libraries. The physical rationale is robust, though issues may arise from limited experimental training data and uncertainties in thermodynamic databases.

directions.direction: Apply in-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) to monitor structural evolution and identify the volume change at melting, connecting diffraction peak shifts and broadening to thermodynamic states.
directions.assessment: Inline XRD measurements during heating yield direct insights into structural and volume changes. Prior evidence (e.g., PMC7412006, PMC8320920) supports this technique, which offers excellent spatial and temporal resolution. The method is applicable across many HEA systems if diffraction peaks remain well defined.

directions.direction: Explore novel processing routes (e.g., rapid solidification or melt-spinning) combined with post-synthesis thermal analysis to indirectly infer fusion properties through microstructural evolution.
directions.assessment: While effective for some HEAs (see PMC11642357), this approach is more indirect and may not capture true equilibrium fusion properties. Its feasibility is high but its direct connection to accurate fusion thermodynamics is less robust than integrated in-situ measurements or simulations.

candidates.hypothesis: Multi-scale MD and hybrid MC/MD simulations incorporating refined interatomic potentials will predict the melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, and liquid-phase entropy of selected refractory HEAs within a ±50 K uncertainty window of experimental DSC measurements.
candidates.intervention: Perform a series of MD and hybrid MC/MD simulations with refined 2NN MEAM or related potentials, gradually heating the system from 300 K to above the melting temperature with 10 K increment steps and appropriate relaxation periods.

candidates.hypothesis: A high-throughput CALPHAD framework augmented with machine learning training on limited experimental DSC datasets will accurately predict the melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of a wide range of HEAs with prediction errors below ±5% relative to experimental values.

candidates.hypothesis: In-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction will detect a quantifiable lattice parameter discontinuity corresponding to a volume change at melting in high-entropy rare earth oxides and metallic HEAs, with observed expansion matching CALPHAD predictions within ±2% error.
